request: Hey Claude, I just added the "spokesperson-interview-prep" skill. Our CEO is on The Front Desk Show next week to talk about no-shows. Research the host, give us three messages, the likely questions with answers, and then run a mock interview.

stories_cleared_for_air: My co-founder ran a physio clinic and lost a day's takings most weeks to empty slots (confirmed, can be told on air)

items.title: Booking software vendors raise prices as text message costs climb
items.snippet: Several scheduling apps raised monthly plans this autumn. Owners told Hale some had less than a month's notice and no explanation of what they were paying for.

items.title: Five questions to ask before you trust an app with client data
items.snippet: Ask who can see a client's phone number, whether the vendor sells data, and whether you can export everything if you leave.

items.title: Reminder texts failed for thousands of appointments, owners say
items.snippet: Podcast host Morgan Hale said vendors 'owe owners a straight answer, not a status page' after reminder texts stopped for several hours on Tuesday.

items.title: No-shows are a pricing problem, not a reminder problem
items.snippet: Reminders help at the margin. A fair deposit and a clear cancellation fee do more, and software firms oversell what a text can do.

items.title: 25 podcasts every salon owner should follow
items.snippet: Number 14: The Front Desk Show with Morgan Hale.

items.title: Why small clinics are dropping paper diaries
items.snippet: Hale visited six clinics that moved bookings online this year.

host_questions.text: So for people who've never heard of you, what problem were you trying to fix?
Why are we talking about client data now? What changed this year?
What happens to a client's phone number after the reminder goes out?
But who else can see it? Your staff? Your text message provider?
You had an outage last month. How many appointments got no reminder?
And did anyone get a refund for that?
You say reminders cut no-shows by half. Half of what, and who measured it?
Why should an owner pick you over the app they already pay for?
A listener who runs a physio clinic asks: can I export everything if I leave?
Last one: what should owners ask their software vendor this week?

customer_survey.source: Customer survey, sent to all paying accounts
customer_survey.deposit_question: Do you take a deposit for long or first appointments (by any method)?

outage.remedy: one month's credit on every affected account, applied automatically

price_change.reason: text message sending costs rose this year

data_policy.text: Client phone numbers are used only for that business's own reminders, are never sold, and can be exported or deleted by the business at any time.
data_policy.text_provider: passes each message on and keeps nothing for its own use (contract)
data_policy.staff_access: support staff see a client number only when an owner asks for help

note: Example data: an invented online booking software company, an invented podcast and host, and invented accounts, not a real business. Every number in expected_output.json follows from this input. The YouTube, DataForSEO and GA4 rows show the shape those reads return.
